page: OVHcloud a10-45 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server deployed under KVM virtualization. The configuration combines an AMD EPYC 9554 processor delivering 30 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading at 3.3 GHz, 42.0 GB of system memory (1.4 GB per core), 400 GB of local SSD storage, and an 8 Gbps network interface. For hardware acceleration, it bundles a single NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPU featuring 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Instruction set support covers AVX-512 extensions including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic engines like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong general and vector-accelerated performance across host resources. The host CPU delivers top-quartile results in stress-ng (3101.99 single-core, 93285.66 multi-core) and Geekbench suites (2100.0 single-core, 16114.0 multi-core), reinforced by high throughput in clang software compilation (43902.0) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (376.71 GB/sec). System memory exhibits top-tier marks in the PassMark memory evaluation (3017.5) and small-block cached read bandwidth, alongside 72.79 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads.

GPU inference benchmarks position the NVIDIA A10 within the top tier for small and mid-range neural networks. For lightweight models (135M), prompt processing reaches 9766.35 tokens per second with generation at 490.91 tokens per second. For 7B parameter models, prompt evaluation hits 2485.10 tokens per second and output generation maintains 91.98 tokens per second. The 24 GB VRAM boundary limits deployment scope, precluding standalone 70B parameter model inference without quantization, offloading, or multi-GPU configurations.

Cost efficiency is focused on targeted AI inference and medium-scale parallel workloads. Providing dedicated CPU cores alongside a dedicated 24 GB enterprise accelerator and bundled local SSD storage gives strong compute density per instance. The primary architectural tradeoff lies in the memory-to-core ratio of 1.4 GB per core and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth (67.99 GB/sec), making it less suitable for high-density in-memory analytics. Appropriate workloads include real-time LLM inference for 7B to 13B architectures, AI-powered image processing, media transcoding, and parallel continuous integration builds.
description: OVHcloud a10-45 is a GPU-accelerated cloud server powered by an AMD EPYC 9554 processor providing 30 dedicated physical cores at 3.3 GHz, 42.0 GB of RAM, a 400 GB local SSD, and an 8 Gbps network interface. Compute capability is paired with a dedicated 24 GB NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPU. Hardware acceleration and AVX-512 extensions yield strong host and accelerator metrics, achieving top-tier inference speeds of 2485.10 tokens per second for prompt processing on 7B models and top-quartile multi-core CPU metrics across Geekbench and stress-ng. System memory bandwidth remains average on large uncached blocks, and the 1.4 GB RAM-per-core ratio limits memory-dense tasks. The a10-45 provides high compute density, serving as an effective platform for small-to-medium LLM inference, computer vision processing, and accelerated build environments.
